meta.title: mm to nm Converter — Millimeter to Nanometer
meta.description: Convert Millimeter (mm) to Nanometer (nm) instantly. 1 mm = 1000000 nm. Free, accurate, browser-based.

content.intro: Convert millimeters (mm) to nanometers (nm) instantly. Both measure length, so the relationship is strictly linear: each millimeter equals 1000000 nanometers. Use the converter above for any value, or read on for the formula, a quick lookup table, and practical tips.
content.result_section: One millimeter is equal to **1000000 nanometers**. To go the other way, one nanometer equals **1.000000e-6 millimeters**. For everyday use, rounding to 2–4 decimal places is usually enough; for engineering or scientific work, keep the full precision shown by the converter.
content.formula_section:
The conversion is a single multiplication:

> nanometers = millimeters × 1000000

Worked example — converting 10 millimeters:

10 × 1000000 = **10000000 nm**.

To invert, divide by 1000000 (or multiply by 1.000000e-6).
content.use_cases:
- Cooking and recipe conversions when switching between metric and imperial measurements.
- Travel planning where signage and maps use different unit systems.
- DIY and home-improvement projects that mix metric materials with imperial tools.
- Fitness tracking when devices report in one system and goals are set in another.
- Shipping and logistics where weight and dimensions drive cost.
content.tips:
Keep the factor handy: 1 mm ≈ 1000000 nm. For rough mental math, round to the nearest sensible digit.

Mind the units. Millimeter and Nanometer both measure length; squared or cubic variants need a different factor (factor², factor³).

When precision matters (engineering, lab work, dosing), avoid rounding mid-calculation — convert once at the final step using the full factor.
content.faq:
**Q:** How many nanometers are in 1 millimeter?
**A:** 1000000 nanometers.

**Q:** What's the formula to convert mm to nm?
**A:** nanometers = millimeters × 1000000.

**Q:** How do I convert nm back to mm?
**A:** Multiply by 1.000000e-6 (or divide by 1000000).

**Q:** Is rounding to 2 decimal places accurate enough?
**A:** For most everyday uses, yes. For scientific or engineering work, use the full precision from the converter.

**Q:** Does this mm to nm converter work offline?
**A:** Yes — all math runs in your browser, no network required after the page loads.
